title: Kakradaa (cog rattle)
summary: The kakradaa is a wooden ratchet of the Winneba asafo groups and their women's adzeba ensembles, said to have come with European sailors. A tongue fixed in a casing turns against a cogwheel on an axle handle, and swinging it round makes a rasping sound.
howToPlay: Three places are lit: the Wheel inside the frame, the Tongue that clicks over its teeth, and the Handle that swings the whole rattle.
A ring closes on the place to strike. The wheel turns faster the longer you keep it going.
Let each whirl run down with the tongue.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It is played in the street processions and the ensembles of the Effutu people of Winneba, where it adds a rasping sound-effect to the drums and songs.
credits: Tradition: the kakradaa; patterns written for this game
